verdict_text: NO. The merge takes the second task vector against the already-modified tensor instead of the unmodified base: it computes `tmp + 0.4 * (ft2 - tmp)` where `tmp = base + 0.4 * (ft1 - base)`, which expands to `base + 0.24*(ft1 - base) + 0.4*(ft2 - base)`, not `base + 0.4*(ft1 - base) + 0.4*(ft2 - base)`. This violates Required result step 2 (and the ordering hazard called out in the Objective), so the 48 merged tensors will exceed the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance. The shared-tensor verification, merged count, and 114-tensor checks are otherwise correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
